about.title: Selma Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Selma's economy runs on agriculture, packing houses, trucking, and the small businesses that line Floral Avenue and Mccall Avenue, which means workplace injuries here often look different than a typical office accident. A forklift mishap at a distribution center, a fall from a ladder at a fruit stand, or a collision involving a delivery truck near Golden State Boulevard can all leave workers hurt and uncertain about their options. In California, workers' compensation is generally the only path against your employer, no matter who was at fault, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate claim against that third party may be possible. Our team can review the full picture of your injury, including any deadlines, and explain what options may apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Selma Workers Choose Us

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Angle
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still be liable. We can help figure out if that applies to your Selma workplace accident.

items.title: Knowing Your Reporting Deadline
items.desc: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. We can help you understand your rights if that becomes a concern.

items.question: I work at a packing facility near Mccall Avenue and got hurt on a machine. Can I sue my employer directly?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, so a direct lawsuit against them typically isn't available. However, if the machine was defective or owned by a third-party contractor, a separate claim outside workers' comp may be possible. We can review the specifics of your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: Generally, you need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days to preserve your workers' comp rights. If a third party is involved, that separate injury claim usually carries a two-year deadline. Timing can vary depending on the facts, so it's worth getting an early review.

items.question: Do you handle claims involving Selma's agricultural or trucking employers specifically?
items.answer: Yes, our team has experience with workplace injuries in industries common to Selma, including agriculture, packing, and trucking, along the Golden State Boulevard and Floral Avenue corridors. Contact us to discuss your situation.
